arxiv-2108-05213.title: Nonlinear dispersion in wave-current interactions
arxiv-2108-05213.creator: Darryl D. Holm, and, Ruiao Hu
arxiv-2108-05213.description: Abstract Via a sequence of approximations of the Lagrangian in Hamilton’s principle for dispersive nonlinear gravity waves we derive a hierarchy of Hamiltonian models for describing wave-current interaction (WCI) in nonlinear dispersive wave dynamics on free surfaces. A subclass of these WCI Hamiltonians admits emergent singular solutions for certain initial conditions.

arxiv-2206-14229.title: Efficiency of random search with space-dependent diffusivity
arxiv-2206-14229.creator: M. A. F. dos Santos 1 , L. Menon Jr. 1 , and C. Anteneodo 1,2
arxiv-2206-14229.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by M. A. F. dos Santos 1 , L. Menon Jr. 1 , and C. Anteneodo 1,2. We address the problem of random search for a target in an environment with space-dependent diffusion coefficient D ⁡ ( x ) D(x) . From a general form of the diffusion differential operator that includes Itô, Stratonovich, and Hänggi-Klimontovich interpretations of the associated stochastic process, we obtain the first-passage time distribution and the search efficiency ℰ = ⟨ 1 / t ⟩ \mathcal{E}=\langle 1/t\rangle .

arxiv-2404-03625.title: Universal Time-Entanglement Trade-off in Open Quantum Systems
arxiv-2404-03625.creator: Andrew Pocklington, Aashish A. Clerk
arxiv-2404-03625.description: Abstract We demonstrate a surprising connection between pure steady state entanglement and relaxation timescales in an extremely broad class of Markovian open systems, where two (possibly many-body) systems A A and B B interact locally with a common dissipative environment. This setup also encompases a broad class of adaptive quantum dynamics based on continuous measurement and feedback.

arxiv-2404-18104.title: The Power of Shallow-depth Toffoli and Qudit Quantum Circuits
arxiv-2404-18104.creator: Alex B. Grilo, Elham Kashefi, Damian Markham, Michael de Oliveira
arxiv-2404-18104.description: Abstract The relevance of shallow-depth quantum circuits has recently increased, mainly due to their applicability to near-term devices. In this context, one of the main goals of quantum circuit complexity is to find problems that can be solved by quantum shallow circuits but require more computational resources classically.

arxiv-2405-18606.title: Track Initialization and Re-Identification for 3D Multi-View Multi-Object Tracking
arxiv-2405-18606.creator: Linh Van Ma, Tran Thien Dat Nguyen, Ba-Ngu Vo, Hyunsung Jang, Moongu Jeon
arxiv-2405-18606.description: Abstract We propose a 3D multi-object tracking (MOT) solution using only 2D detections from monocular cameras, which automatically initiates/terminates tracks as well as resolves track appearance-reappearance and occlusions. Moreover, this approach does not require detector retraining when cameras are reconfigured but only the camera matrices of reconfigured cameras need to be updated.

arxiv-2412-12613.title: Energy scaling in a compact bulk multi-pass cell enabled by Laguerre-Gaussian single-vortex beams
arxiv-2412-12613.creator: V. Koltalo *, S. Westerberg, M. Redon, G. Beaufort, A.-K. Raab, C. Guo, C. L. Arnold, A.-L. Viotti *
arxiv-2412-12613.description: Abstract We report pulse energy scaling enabled by the use of Laguerre-Gaussian single-vortex ( LG 0 , l \text{LG}_{0,l} ) beams for spectral broadening in a sub-40 cm long Herriott-type bulk multi-pass cell. Beams with orders l = 1 − 3 {l=1-3} are generated by a spatial light modulator, which facilitates rapid and precise reconfiguration of the experimental conditions.

arxiv-2503-20149.title: Treatment Effects Inference with High-Dimensional Instruments and Control Variables
arxiv-2503-20149.creator: Xiduo Chen, Xingdong Feng, Antonio F. Galvao, Yeheng Ge
arxiv-2503-20149.description: Abstract Obtaining valid treatment effect inference remains a challenging problem when dealing with numerous instruments and non-sparse control variables. In this paper, we propose a novel ridge regularization-based instrumental variables method for estimation and inference in the presence of both high-dimensional instrumental variables and high-dimensional control variables. These methods are applicable both with and without sparsity assumptions.

arxiv-2507-15901.title: Advancing Responsible Innovation in Agentic AI: A study of Ethical Frameworks for Household Automation
arxiv-2507-15901.creator: Joydeep Chandra, Satyam Kumar Navneet
arxiv-2507-15901.description: Abstract The implementation of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in household environments, especially in the form of proactive autonomous agents, brings about possibilities of comfort and attention as well as it comes with intra or extramural ethical challenges. This article analyzes agentic AI and its applications, focusing on its move from reactive to proactive autonomy, privacy, fairness and user control.

pmc-10689049.title: Toxicology Test Results for Public Health Surveillance of the Opioid Epidemic: Retrospective Analysis
pmc-10689049.creator: Titus Schleyer, Bill Robinson, Samir Parmar, Diane Janowiak, P Joseph Gibson, Val Spangler
pmc-10689049.description: BackgroundAddressing the opioid epidemic requires timely insights into population-level factors, such as trends in prevalence of legal and illegal substances, overdoses, and deaths.ObjectiveThis study aimed to examine whether toxicology test results of living individuals from a variety of sources could be useful in surveilling the opioid epidemic.

pmc-11579972.title: A Matter of Charge: Electrostatically Tuned Coassembly of Amphiphilic Peptides
pmc-11579972.creator: Elad Arad, Topaz Levi, Gal Yosefi, Itamar Kass, Ifat Cohen‐Erez, Ziv Azoulay, Ronit Bitton, Raz Jelinek, Hanna Rapaport
pmc-11579972.description: Coassembly of peptide biomaterials offers a compelling avenue to broaden the spectrum of hierarchically ordered supramolecular nanoscale structures that may be relevant for biomedical and biotechnological applications. In this work coassemblies of amphiphilic and oppositely charged, anionic and cationic, β‐sheet peptides are studied, which may give rise to a diverse range of coassembled forms.

pmc-11643958.title: City Residents Play a Pivotal Role in Managing Global Food Security While Improving Human Health and Minimizing Environmental Footprints
pmc-11643958.creator: Jan-Olof Drangert, Joseph Sharkey
pmc-11643958.description: Background/Objectives: Improved global data allow for a new understanding of what impact the food we produce, eat and dispose of has on the environment, human health and Nature’s resources. The overall goal is to guide decision-makers and individuals by providing in-depth knowledge about the effects of their dietary preferences on human and environmental health.

pmc-12748865.title: Decoupled Antarctic and Subarctic export productivity under intensified Southern Hemisphere westerlies during the last interglacial
pmc-12748865.creator: Lijuan Lu, Qinghua Yang, Marcus Gutjahr, Qian Shi, Renhao Wu, Huang Huang, Yiming Luo, Hu Yang, Zhaoyang Song, Liu Jiping, Shuh-Ji Kao
pmc-12748865.description: The Last Interglacial (128–113 ka B.P.) provides key insights into climate-carbon interactions under warm, high-CO2 conditions. While Antarctic temperature-driven Southern Ocean ventilation has been proposed to modulate atmospheric CO2, role of Southern Hemisphere westerlies (SHW) remains unclear. Here we synthesize 15 Antarctic and 5 subarctic Pacific export productivity records over two glacial-interglacial cycles.

pmc-13051816.title: Thermodynamic and Transport Properties of Alkanes (C n H2n+2; n = 5–8)
pmc-13051816.creator: Deependra Awasthi, Narayan Gautam, Shyam P Khanal, Rajendra Prasad Koirala, Narayan P Adhikari
pmc-13051816.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). In the present work, we have utilized “alchemical” approaches to study the thermodynamic properties of four alkane molecules: pentane, hexane, heptane, and octane in water. We have used thermodynamic integration (TI) and free energy perturbation (FEP) based methods: TI, TI‐cubic, Bennett acceptance ration (BAR), and Multistate Bennett acceptance ratio (MBAR)to estimate the solvation free energy of alkane molecules in water at 300 K for 21 distinct coupling parameter values (λ).

pmc-13160424.title: An osteoporotic bone model: developing and validating an ex-vivo bone demineralization protocol
pmc-13160424.creator: Fahad Alabdah, Adel Alshammari, Araida Hidalgo-Bastida, Glen Cooper
pmc-13160424.description: Studies estimate that there are 500 million osteoporotic patients worldwide. Osteoporosis leads to 2.7 million hip fractures annually. These fractures usually require synthetic implants known as total hip replacement. Orthopedic implant development is an ongoing process, which requires numerous tests to evaluate their feasibility, in addition to the International Standards Organization regulatory tests.

pmc-13246771.title: Heterodera schachtii enolase does not elicit canonical immune responses in Arabidopsis thaliana
pmc-13246771.creator: Maximilian F Euler, Neil Pep Dave N Sumaya, Seema Aslam, Johannes Lerch, Badou Mendy, Florian M W Grundler
pmc-13246771.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Enolase (2-phospho-D-glycerate hydrolase, EC 4.2.1.11) is a conserved glycolytic enzyme that catalyzes the reversible dehydration of 2-phosphoglycerate to phosphoenolpyruvate. In animal- and entomopathogenic nematodes, enolase has been shown to interact with host organisms and activate immune responses. In the plant-parasitic cyst nematode Heterodera schachtii, an established model species, enolase is hypothesized to be similarly exposed to host plant tissues during infection, based on its identification in the secretomes of related plant-parasitic nematodes.

pmc-13327214.title: Elimination Profile of Deflazacort and Metabolites in Urine and Plasma Following Oral Administration: Relevance to Sports Drug Testing
pmc-13327214.creator: Sergi Coll, Claudia Bressan, Núria Monfort, Ana Aldea‐Perona, Marcel·lí Carbó, Rosa Ventura
pmc-13327214.description: Deflazacort (DEF) is a glucocorticoid prohibited in sports competitions when orally administered. This study aimed to assess the urinary and plasma excretion profiles of DEF and its metabolites after a single oral administration to verify the World Anti‐Doping Agency's minimum reporting level (MRL) of 30 ng/mL to detect administration of DEF.

pmc-13380918.title: Comparative Risk of Psoriatic Arthritis in Type 2 Diabetes: An Emulated Target Trial of SGLT2 Inhibitors vs. GLP-1 Receptor Agonists
pmc-13380918.creator: Fu-Shun Yen, Shiow-Ing Wang, Chii-Min Hwu, Kai-Yang Chen, Chih-Cheng Hsu, James Cheng-Chung Wei
pmc-13380918.description: BackgroundPatients with psoriatic arthritis (PsA) have a higher prevalence of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and cardiovascular events. They also experience increased absenteeism and reduced work productivity, all of which can negatively affect both life expectancy and quality of life.
